method: What drives a negative price is the share of demand left once solar, wind and nuclear are served:   R = (load − solar − wind − nuclear) ÷ load          (RTE éCO2mix actuals, data/history/fr_hourly) nuclear = the nuclear AVAILABLE (highest hourly output of the week before: its output drops when prices go negative, so the output itself hides the surplus). The same share for Germany (exports), the solar share, weekend, hour and month feed a logistic regression on the last three years, recent days weighing more (half-life one year: batteries and flexible demand change the market).
source: RTE éCO2mix (history) · ENTSO-E day-ahead forecasts via Energy-Charts · ENTSO-E day-ahead prices
